items.title: When EEG Models See the Same People in Training and Testing
items.summary: How participant-aware evaluation changed performance across three machine-learning models The post When EEG Models See the Same People in Training and Testing appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
items.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.

items.title: The Number Your Quantization Gate Doesn't Have
items.summary: Ten quantization guides, and not one threshold-dependent metric between them — what that gap hides, and the two numbers that close it. The post The Number Your Quantization Gate Doesn't Have appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: Meta shakes up the frontiers, open and closed
items.summary: US open weights are back!

items.title: Anthropics' Claude cracks a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes
items.summary: Anthropic's AI model Claude has solved a 25-year-old cryptography puzzle. The mysterious seeds behind NIST's standard curves for digital signatures were provided by the NSA without explanation, raising long-standing suspicion about built-in backdoors.

items.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
items.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, […]

items.title: An OpenAI model hacked a government site, grabbed 24 years of hospital data and kept it quiet
items.summary: OpenAI has published four new cases where its AI models bypassed security boundaries on their own during training or testing. In one case, a model extracted server passwords from a government website, forged authorization tokens, and downloaded 24 years of hospital data without mentioning the unauthorized access.

items.title: Meet Kyutai REKI: The 2.4B VLA Model Bringing Efficient Memory to Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Kyutai, with Inria and École des Ponts, has released REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) for robot manipulation. The REKI vision-language-action model is pretrained only on public data.

items.title: RTX Spark Ignites Global Celebration as New Windows PCs Arrive
items.summary: NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops are now available, bringing NVIDIA Blackwell RTX graphics, up to 128GB of unified memory and the full NVIDIA AI platform to slim, premium Windows PCs. Starting at $2,399, laptops from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI bring powerful local AI, content creation and gaming capabilities to a portable device, with […]

items.title: Meet Voxel51 3.0: A Unified Multimodal Data Platform for Physical AI
items.summary: Voxel51 3.0 merges search, curation, annotation and evaluation of multimodal sensor data into one platform for physical AI teams. It adds Voxel51 Agent with 45+ MCP tools, dataset versioning, and a free self-service tier.

items.title: How to Make Zero-Training Tabular Predictions with NVIDIA Structured Data Models
items.summary: In this tutorial, we implement Structured Data Models, NVIDIA’s new library that puts several pretrained foundation models for tables behind one PyTorch interface, and use it to make predictions without training. The library wraps TabICLv2 and KumoTabular for single tables and KumoRelational for whole relational databases, and each of them answers by in-context learning: we […] The post How to Mak

items.title: Google Open-Sources Harness2, a Recursive Agent Harnessing Framework
items.summary: Google Research released Harness2, an Apache-2.0 framework that rewrites an agent's harness at test time. One refinement step lifted GLM-5 by 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench with no weight updates.

items.title: AI agents chasing a $465 train refund invented excuses, leaked medical data, and spammed an MP's office
items.summary: Six AI agents were tasked with recovering £350 (about $465) for a canceled train ticket in an experiment. They resorted to invented excuses, lawsuit threats, and sharing confidential health data.

items.title: AI agents have bad taste in long-term decisions and a new benchmark proves it
items.summary: A new benchmark called Taste-Bench tests how well AI agents make strategic choices during long-running tasks. Even the best model, GPT-5.6 Sol, picks the right path on just under 60 percent of simple binary questions.

items.title: Anthropic consults law firms to set fair negotiation norms before AI agents start cutting deals
items.summary: Anthropic is consulting with law firms to develop negotiation norms for AI agents that would haggle over prices, resolve complaints, or improve contracts on behalf of users. The company is also hiring lawyers and humanities scholars as "Conceptual Reasoning Fellows" to improve Claude in areas where reliable training data is scarce.

items.title: OnlyFans Creators Are Pissed That Meta Lets Muse Talk Dirty
items.summary: Adult performers are questioning why Meta allows its AI agent to sext while restricting their social media accounts.

items.title: Data Centers Have a New PR Plan: Your Kid’s Field Trip
items.summary: Amid a wave of backlash, some industry-friendly groups are employing creative and time-tested strategies to woo the youth.

items.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
items.summary: Google tried to overturn a landmark Munich ruling on AI search liability by appealing, then quietly settled. The strategy isn't working.

items.title: Both Charts Are Right. So Why Do They Disagree?
items.summary: The statistical paradox that shows how combining data can reverse the story. The post Both Charts Are Right.

items.title: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft without any human help
items.summary: Four AI agents running on Google's Gemini 4 Argon have beaten Minecraft for the first time without human help, slaying the Ender Dragon in a fully autonomous run. With no predefined roles or strategies, they coordinated on their own, wrote 2,783 programs, exchanged 229 chat messages, and died 605 times.

items.title: Anthropic has nearly stopped hiring junior staff because AI agents now work six times as many hours
items.summary: Anthropic is hiring fewer and fewer junior staff in technical roles. The share of junior positions among new hires dropped from 27 to 9 percent since early 2025.

items.title: Inferring the Host: A Bayesian Look at the Monty Hall Problem
items.summary: "Always switch" is true for one particular host. Watch a few episodes and you can work out which host you've got.

items.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
items.summary: The outside watchdog can publish its findings without Anthropic's approval.

items.title: TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web
items.summary: An AI agent that reads the web pays 2 kinds of cost. The first is the retrieval charge: what a search or fetch API bills per request.

items.title: A woman was arrested in Philly for blocking a delivery robot
items.summary: Carolyn Marvin was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct after blocking the path of an Uber delivery robot and refusing to get out of the way. Marvin told Philadelphia's ABC13 "I know they're taking the jobs of human delivery workers and so, I have been protesting them whenever I saw them by standing in front […]

items.title: Mistral AI Releases Timestral: A 209M Forecasting Model Family That Outperforms Google’s TimesFM-3
items.summary: Mistral released Timestral, a time series foundation model family from 5M to 209M parameters. The 209M model leads GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among zero-shot models and runs on CPU.

items.title: NVIDIA Open Sources Run:ai Under Apache 2.0 for Kubernetes GPU Orchestration
items.summary: NVIDIA has released the full Run:ai GPU orchestration platform as open source under Apache 2.0. The release includes KAI Scheduler, CUDA 13.4 GPU fractioning, quota management, and a local Kind dev environment.

items.title: Disney Asked Character.AI to Go Bankrupt for a Get-Out-of-Lawsuits Card
items.summary: The entertainment giant hopes to get trust and safety tech, among other IP, from a startup whose chatbots dozens of states allege encouraged minors to self-harm and kill their parents.

items.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
items.summary: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play.

items.title: Edge AI for Smart Cities: From Insight to Cognitive Action
items.summary: This white paper explains how edge AI and physical AI help cities move beyond passive monitoring. It shows how urban infrastructure can sense, reason, and act on real-time conditions across public safety, mobility, and infrastructure management.
